turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_dn_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`, `poscar`
    (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `dn` (the birefringence at
    1064 nm, dimensionless).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST
birefringence at 1064 nm, then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c012, c047, c003, c031,
c088".
turns.answer_text:
I looked for candidates that match the high-`dn` motifs in the training set: low-symmetry, strongly anisotropic structures with heavy/polarizable anions or lone-pair/heavy cations. The strongest training precedents are alkali pnictide frameworks (`Rb8Sb8`, `Cs8Sb8`), chalcogen-rich low-dimensional compounds (`Tl8Te12`, `Cs4Cu4Se16`, `Ba2Te6`), distorted heavy halide frameworks (`RbSnBr3`), and the `Nb–Ag–P–S` framework around `dn ≈ 0.29`.

Most promising candidates:

- `c007` (`Rb8As8`): close structural analogue of the very high-birefringence `Rb8Sb8`/`Cs8Sb8` family; As is lighter than Sb but the framework motif is highly favorable.
- `c089` (`Cs8Se12`): chalcogen-rich, anisotropic polyselenide-like structure, related in spirit to very high chalcogen-rich training compounds.
- `c039` (`Rb4Ge4I12`): distorted heavy iodide framework; analogous to high `RbSnBr3`, with very polarizable I.
- `c079` (`Ba4Ge2Te5Se3`): Te/Se-rich, low-symmetry chalcogenide; resembles high-birefringence Te-chain/polychalcogenide chemistry such as `Ba2Te6`.
- `c049` (`Rb1 Nb4 Ag1 P2 S20`): near-direct analogue of training `K1 Nb4 Ag1 P2 S20` with `dn ≈ 0.295`, so a robust high pick.

Final: c007, c089, c039, c079, c049
